title: Spindizzy
build: Electric Dreams' 1986 PAL disk, the G64 spindizzy[electric_dreams_1986](pal) from the C64 Preservation Project collection on the Internet Archive (SHA-256 07cf3a77…7de2d8)

tools.host: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04.5 cloud container, four cores, no display

accuracy.note: 60 of 303 hand-written comments and 20 of 518 generated ones; 21.2 % weighted by stratum
the room renderer, the sound effects, the password check and the inhabitants' speeds, run on the game's own code; steer_speed's direction flag

exclude: zero page, the stack and the KERNAL's work area: the game's variables, cleared by start_game_image ($02-$81) and new_game; the boot file SPINDIZZY loads over $02A7-$0303 and is the loader, outside the analysis

not the game's: start_game_image copies 64 pages from $1400 to $0400, which takes in whatever RAM held at $4D01-$53FF past the end of SPIN4; above that, SPIN4's own bytes are left where they loaded ($1400-$4D00) and only the copy at $0400 is read
the tile buffer ($AA80-$B6FF, 25 rows of 16 places of 8 bytes) and the room grid ($B700-$B8FF), rebuilt for every room; SPIN3 loads them as $EA filler

run-time state: the jewels collected ($C1C0-$C1DF, a bit each), the piece table at $C200, the sprite slots at $C280-$C2BF and the work cells and sprite masks at $C300-$C37F; SPIN3 loads leftover bytes there that new_game and the room builder overwrite
the colour matrix of the bitmap screen and the sprite pointers at $C7F8, drawn by the game
the sprite shapes the game builds at run time (pointers $30-$3F); SPIN3 loads zeros there
the bitmap, drawn by the game; under the KERNAL ROM
